utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, I'm sorry to have kept you this morning, but there were matters I had to attend to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Of course. Your Honour, the position on the witnesses is there are three witnesses today, two short ones and one much more substantial one. The two short ones are, I hope, each in the process of reviewing in order to approve and initial, or whatever, their summaries in order that they may be taken more swiftly than formally, and I'm not sure either is yet immediately ready. So there may be other matters we can conveniently deal with straight away. First, Mr. Sayers tells me that when I told you yesterday the map that Mr. Hamill produced was in the Zenica binder, I was wrong. It was indexed but not in the binder. Naturally, I apologise for that. I'm sorry that that was incorrect when stated by me. The second thing that we might conveniently deal with, I suppose, straight away, is the question of the statements of the Witness AO that were produced, and you've seen the letter that was produced yesterday. The position on all that is, I suppose, as follows, at least the recent history of that is as follows: In cross-examination, it became quite clear that the witness had given another statement or statements. Indeed, I think right at the beginning, he spoke of a statement either to the OTP or to the village or to the town. Then later on, he was cross-examined really in quite a focused way by Mr. Naumovski, being pretty apparent to us and I think to the witness, as he subsequently confirmed when speaking to the investigator after evidence, it became pretty obvious that they had information on him. And there was some focused cross-examination on other earlier statements. It rather looked as though they might actually have had information upon the detail of one of those statements, an impression which, when the statement eventually came to light, may have been confirmed, because there was a match of detail put with detail in the statement. In any event, after he had concluded his evidence, Ms. Taylor spoke to him and confirmed that which appeared, that he had spoken to other people. Not something that he ever kept back from us; just something that hadn't emerged. And I think he explained to you how he'd given answers to lots of people, maybe couldn't remember the circumstances or how he came to sign them, at a time shortly before, I think, Your Honour cut short his cross-examination and said you'd had enough on that. In any event, a further search was conducted by Ms. Taylor and then by others. The statements were found, they being the sort of statement that, knowing of their existence, we would look for again. They were immediately handed over. One of them exists in English and in B/C/S; and the other one, at the moment, only in B/C/S. A proper translation is being sought for it. So that's the history of that. Of course, I'm sorry they weren't found before, but as soon as they were found, they were handed over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think the matter of importance is this: Why weren't they found before?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, they weren't found before because they didn't turn up in the searches before. Indeed I understand that the same search duplicated since doesn't turn -- or a search duplicated since doesn't turn the document up again. These things are not perfect. Also, the original search found the material -- I think finds it in a bulk of material; that is, it's not searched under the name and turns up immediately under the name. It turns up in a bulk of other material. So that's the reason for it. There's every effort made to find material that's relevant. It's only because of the redoubled efforts that I'm happy to say we found it this time. It seems, in any event, that the Defence had some knowledge from some source of that statement or some account of it. They have now been handed over and there it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sayers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. President, let me just say at this stage of the case we're sort of resigned to this kind of treatment by the Prosecution, without meaning any aspersions on anyone. The map incident yesterday, the delivery of statements of two of the witnesses today at 9.00 a.m. We still haven't got a statement from the third witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, to be fair about the statements, those are the summaries you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This is a slightly different point. You've had the statements of the witnesses, no doubt, in the proper time. The difficulty about the summaries, of course, is they can only be compiled when the witnesses are here. So I think it's not fair to criticise the Prosecution on that ground. However, of course, the matter we're dealing with is totally different.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The Court will no doubt recall that an application was made to add this witness to the witness list. I believe it was on January the 31st, but I may be wrong on the date. That's my recollection. The reason for the addition of this witness to the witness list was that the identity of this witness was supposedly unknown to the Prosecution, unknown to the Prosecution, and they had only recently come into possession, we were told, of a statement apparently from NordBat. I will say, parenthetically, we have requested the statement -- the entire statement from NordBat, as the Court knows, and treaties in that regard have simply been ignored. Now, it turns out that the statements from this witness existed in the Prosecution's databases all the time. That's a very significant matter of concern for us, but it's not nearly as significant as disclosing these materials to us after the witness has already testified, because the statements -- I'm sure the Court has had the chance to review them -- display a level of mendacity which is pretty self-evident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I can say I have merely looked at those cursorily, and it may be of assistance if you point to the matters you used in cross-examination, because that, of course, is the matter we are going to have to consider.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: On page 1 it is said by this witness that various forms of cooperation with parts of the so-called Republika Srpska were quite normal. The Court will recall that he said something completely different in his direct-examination and cross-examination. On page 3, Your Honour, this witness says: "My subsequent involvement in the HVO Special Purpose Unit" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just let me find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. It's about two inches down from the top of the typed matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: "... so-called Specijalka in Vares was prompted by purely personal interests." Now, the Court will recall that the witness completely abjured any connection with the HVO in unequivocal, undiluted terms. He then goes on, approximately three inches up from the bottom of that paragraph, Your Honour, to say, "When I joined the Specijalka, my war duties allowed me to observe all the illegal activities carried out by current officials and institutions in Vares ..." and then goes on to talk about those black-market activities --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let me find that. Which paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Well, the pages are not numbered, Your Honour, but at the bottom of the page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You've got the Prosecution numbers, or at least I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Number 00323996, that's the page number, and then the first full paragraph on the page, about three inches up from the bottom of the paragraph, or two inches, he says: "When I joined the Specijalka, my war duties ..." and goes on to describe them. He then goes on to say, at the bottom of that paragraph, Your Honour, that he carried out certain transactions in relation to these illegal activities for his own personal benefit. Then, Your Honour, about one inch up from the bottom of the last paragraph, I want to draw the Court's attention to something, and admittedly, I haven't had a considerable opportunity to scrutinise this because I've been busy preparing for other witnesses, but let me just say, my recollection of what the witness said was as follows: He said, "As an HOS member, I was a trusted confidante of Ivica Rajic, and that's why I was included in these planning sessions, and I was able to hear a telephone conversation and see an order that was signed by Boban, Kordic, and/or Praljak." Here he says he was taken out of bed by the HVO military police on the orders of Rajic, shown a document from General Praljak, not from Mr. Kordic, and then he goes on, at the top of the next page, to say that he was kept in some kind of detention until the morning. An absolutely completely different story from that which he told to the Court in direct examination and cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, he does say: "I think these facts help to explain his trust in me."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Having been arrested, Your Honour, I -- well, I understand what the witness says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: He says that he was kept in detention; he made no mention of that, of course, during his examination-in-chief or cross-examination. And then, of course, one thing that I do want to emphasise is that the name Kordic doesn't appear, as far as I'm aware, in either of these two statements, not one of them, and I will defer to my colleague Mr. Naumovski with respect to the Croatian statements since I do not read that language.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will you slow down, Mr. Sayers, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Right. He also says, on page 00323997, that during the night, while he was staying in the headquarters, he learned during the night that Ivica Rajic's extremists, who made up the formations of Maturice, Sijuski, and Apostoli, had been ordered to take Stupni Do. That is completely different from what he said relating to a meeting that occurred, by his account, completely vallecularly, three days early, on October the 20th. Needless to say, Your Honour -- and I will, as I say, defer to my colleague Mr. Naumovski -- the possession of these statements, which, I want to emphasise, I've never seen before and have never even heard about before, they were disclosed to us by the Prosecution. We think that the only --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You say you haven't. Have the Defence generally known of these matters?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: As I said, I will yield the floor to Mr. Naumovski so he can tell you for himself. But I can tell you that our databases, and we try to keep these fairly carefully, have absolutely no copies of these, or even references to them or even intimations that they existed. Under these circumstances, I would submit that the only possible course for the Court to take would be to strike the testimony of this witness altogether. With that said, let me hand over the floor to Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Sayers, before you do that, let's consider the position. Effectively it is this: that there is material here which should have been disclosed to you before you cross-examined the witness, and it wasn't, the witness having given evidence, and this is material which you say goes very much to his credibility. That being so, the question is what should be done? One course, as you suggest or submit, is that we should simply disregard all his evidence. Another course is, of course, that we now have this material and we can take it into consideration when considering what weight, if any, to give his evidence. The third course, I suppose, is that he is brought back at some stage for cross-examination on these statements. That would probably have to be in the rebuttal stage of the case. I'm thinking aloud. I don't know if there are any other courses which suggest themselves to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Sayers. Mr. Naumovski, we've heard what Mr. Sayers has said. You need not repeat that; I'm sure you wouldn't. It's suggested that you may have had some knowledge of these statements. If you want to deal with that suggestion, of course you may.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you for allowing me to say a few words as well. I can only confirm that I had absolutely no knowledge of these statements, neither I nor any member of our team. Since he spent some time in the NordBat, it was only natural that he was questioned subsequently by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and that is why he confirmed these statements before this Honourable Court. I don't want to repeat what my colleague Mr. Sayers said. The other statement will be translated for you as well, and I believe that you will see for yourselves what I tried to show to the Court throughout the cross-examination, and that is what kind of a person we are dealing with. It is the credibility of this witness that is questionable, and this statement shows it best of all. He admits here that he was involved in private business for his own benefit, and then also for that firm Jakici, which he denied here when testifying before you. So this was his private interest. Just a detail. You may recall the question I put in connection with something that the priest Piplica asked him to do, and you asked me why I was putting that question, you asked me why I was putting this question. He abused this priest. He did not deliver the goods he was supposed to deliver, he denied that, and he also gave himself credit for certain things. This is page --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Naumovski has to slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Could you slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. So, Your Honours, on page 00323998, in the middle paragraph, in the lower half of the page, it is obvious that he was told that he was supposed to deliver 67 tonnes of goods to the priest in Vares, and those goods never arrived. So he actually confirms this, although he denied it while testifying here. I don't want to go into other details. Your Honours will see this for yourselves, but there are two things I wish to say. First of all, we had absolutely no knowledge whatsoever concerning his statements. These were statements that were made to the authorities of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and, regrettably, we have no access to these sources. Secondly, my opinion is, and the Defence proposal is, that as far as we are concerned, the testimony of this witness can simply, and should simply be rejected, because you will see this for yourselves and you will see how questionable his credibility is, and thereby everything that he said is questionable. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, since it was somehow implied that the Defence might have had such statements of this witness, the Cerkez Defence also have never seen such statements, and as a matter of principle, we do support the point of view of the other Defence. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, I tell you what we have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The justice of the case requires that this witness, in due course, return to be tested on those matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I entirely agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It may be the simplest if that is done during the course of the rebuttal case. He should be brought back.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll make arrangements. I was going to say that it would be quite wrong to strike the witness's evidence, he having come here and he not having a chance to deal with these matters. He left. Of course, he was concerned, incidentally, because his name had been used in court. That didn't emerge to us because it doesn't come through on the transcript. But we've monitored or had monitored -- or somebody has monitored the press and it appears that his name hasn't gone out so far. So with luck that won't affect his willingness to attend. Of course, he left with the intention of finding some of the documents he said he was going to try and find for us. So his being recalled is an entirely proper course and we'll make arrangements in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We'll make that order, that the Prosecution -- it's your responsibility, Mr. Nice, to recall him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What I was hoping for today was that we would be able to fit in all the administrative matters as soon as possible, leaving a clear period of time for the substantial witness, but I gather Mr. Scott's witness is now ready to give evidence, and it may be prudent for that witness to be taken now, sensible for that witness to be taken now. I'll go and check on the position of the second short witness whom I'm taking. It's possible that if we can dispose of both of those witnesses in, I don't know, an hour or thereabouts, that will give the balance of the morning, but for other administrative matters, to the substantial witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. There is one matter which -- the affidavits on which we're having some work done and research done, and we're not in a position to take them yet. If necessary, we shall have to sit tomorrow morning, but we'll see how it goes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know whether it is a proper moment, but just in case, I would like to stay with the objections that I raised yesterday to have a witness earlier listed under number 10 of the list of the transcripts, to have him today as a witness. It is, by my opinion -- I will not repeat myself basically on the arguments I had yesterday. I just checked how much material it is. I did my best, but that is still not fair to bring a witness -- to announce to the Defence in the afternoon, on the eve of the testimony of such a voluminous testimony, and in such a difficult moment when we are really fighting with tonnes of documents and many, many issues which should be discussed with this Chamber on the last day of the Prosecution case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Kovacic, as I said yesterday when dealing with the application, if you haven't had time to prepare for cross-examination, then we will consider postponing your cross-examination until tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I appreciate that. That will give me at least some additional time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's see how we get on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Is there an application in relation to the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, there is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It was handed in.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. May it please the Court. There is an application. If we could go into private session for a moment. Perhaps it's not necessary, to mention the witness's name. The Court has the papers and knows who is being discussed, although it would probably be preferable if it were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We should go into private session for this purpose.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Pseudonym for this witness is Witness AQ.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you'd like to take a seat. Examined by Mr. Scott:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the usher is putting in front of you a paper with your name on it. For purposes of affording you protection, we do not want you to state your name out loud in court, but will you simply, for purposes of identification, look at that paper and answer yes or no: Is that your name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Witness, your request for protection has been granted, just so you know and can know that at the outset. You will be referred to in court today as Witness AQ. So if I refer to you as Witness AQ, you'll know that's why, not out of any discourtesy. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness speak up, please? We cannot hear her at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you'll have to speak a little louder, please, for the purposes of the record. Maybe you can -- let me ask for purposes of translation, let me ask my last question. Did you understand, Witness AQ, that I'll be referring to you this morning as Witness AQ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Usher, if you could possibly move this big microphone. Sorry, Your Honour. It's a bit disconcerting to look at the witness and have her -- that's fine. I would like to be able to see the witness. Thank you, usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AQ, first I would like for you to confirm for the record, in the course of coming to The Hague and having been in The Hague for the last few days, were you provided a proposed outline or summary, if you will, of your anticipated testimony today, and did you have a chance to review and sign that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if you could put this before the witness, please. For purposes of the record, Your Honour, we would have this identified as Z2817.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think there's an objection to this particular summary being --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There is an objection to this summary being admitted. The witness can have it in front of her. If necessary, we'll review the position at the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. I wasn't moving it other than to identify it for purposes of the record. A document has been placed in front of her that has been tentatively identified as 2817. I understand at this point it's not admitted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AQ, if you could please turn to the last page of that item, the page 7. Does that page 7 have your signature and today's date, indicating that the statement -- this statement is true and correct to the best of your knowledge, information, and belief?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, Witness AQ, is it correct that in October 1992, you and your family moved to Ahmici? You lived in about the middle of the village, between the upper and lower mosque?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Around June or July of 1992, the HVO established a checkpoint on the road going into Ahmici, and an anti-aircraft machine-gun was placed there which was aimed at Ahmici. Is that correct, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first attack on Ahmici was on the 20th of October, 1992. It was primarily an artillery attack meant to scare the Muslims or to see how they would react. There were also HVO soldiers in the lower part of the village who set some houses on fire. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the shelling on 20th of October, the minaret on the lower mosque in Ahmici was hit. There were later statements on Croat and Bosnian Croat television to the effect that the mosque was shelled because Muslim snipers were firing from the mosque. First of all, do you recall that, that information up to that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you believe, or to your knowledge, as a resident of the village, that there were snipers or had been snipers posted, if you will, on the minaret?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: No, there were not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At no time during your residence in the village were you aware, had seen, or heard of any Bosniak snipers being positioned on the mosque, on the minaret?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were no ABiH or TO units, formations, or positions in Ahmici in October 1992 when it was attacked; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, can you confirm, Witness AQ, that on that day or about that day, you also had occasion to travel in the area, that you and your husband travelled to Poculica, and during that travel, if you will, neither your husband nor you saw any gatherings or formations of ABiH or TO soldiers in the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: We did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct, Witness, that you understood, around the time of this first attack on Ahmici, that is, October 1992, that the HVO had been very angry around that time because some HVO vehicles had been stopped by the Bosniaks near Ahmici on their way to -- I think it was actually Novi Travnik. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of this attack in October, one Bosniak man was killed, about seven houses were burned, and approximately ten barns destroyed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AQ, for the next series of questions, I'm going to ask you if you can speak to the Court more in your own words. I want to direct your attention to the 15th of April, 1993. This was a time of Easter that year; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you relate to the Court any thing or person that you saw on television on the 15th of April, 1993? Just describe what you saw, who you were with at the time, and any thoughts or reactions you may have had to what you saw on TV.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: That day I, my husband, his sister, and my three-year-old son were at home. All the day on Busovaca Television, the Busovaca Television was transmitting the Easter celebrations in Busovaca. When the programme would be finished on Busovaca Television, the Vitez Television would take it over and then transmit it again. Dario Kordic spoke on that occasion. He invited the Croat people to an uprising, to rally to the defence against Muslim forces. The units of the BH army were not called by him the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; they called them Muslim forces. From what he said, it was evident that he was inviting to an armed insurgence. He said that they were better armed than the Muslims, and that meant that he was proclaiming war. My husband believed what he had said, that something was really in the offing, but I could not believe it, because I had grown up in an environment where there were many Croats, and we've never had any problem. So I believe that it wasn't all that simple, to call people, to rise and go to war, because we were already at war with the Serbs. Unfortunately, it did, indeed, come true, and after the 16th of April, I knew that all that Kordic had stated that day was true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AQ, you saw this speech, or similar speeches throughout the course of the 15th of April; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was essentially repeatedly broadcast throughout the day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me direct you, please. During your time in The Hague --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps you'll let me approach it this way. Let me first inform the Court, and then I'll ask the witness. In the course of her being here, Your Honour, she was shown Prosecution Exhibit Z665, which is admitted in evidence and was the press conference showing Dario Kordic, Tihomir Blaskic, and Kostroman on the 15th of April, 1993. The Court may recall having seen that on at least one occasion during the trial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AQ, let me ask you, when you were shown a tape of a speech involving Mr. Kordic on the 15th of April, 1993, was that the same speech that you've related to the Court just a moment ago, or was there a different speech?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: It was that very speech.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of all the speeches you heard during the course of that day, was it the same broadcast, or were there different speeches by Mr. Kordic being broadcast, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Different speeches. It was a live transmission from the Easter festival, and then there was this other speech. When I saw the tape, I just remembered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the speech, did Mr. Kordic say something to the effect that Busovaca was the heart of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did ask that my learned colleague not ask leading questions in this matter. That was one of the things.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. I think we've covered most things down through paragraph 13, I think, or at least 12.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go on to paragraph 13. Before this occasion, on the 15th of April, had you seen any of these men -- Dario Kordic, Ignac Kostroman, Tihomir Blaskic -- on television before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any particular understanding of the relationship between those three men? I don't necessarily mean a personal relationship, but the relationship as part of a political or military group.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: From what one could see in these recordings of their press conferences, one could see that they were very closely linked and that they were cooperating very well amongst themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After Ahmici, did you form any conclusions as to how the attack on Ahmici had come about, in terms of the organisation and execution of that attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: I think that it had all been -- that it was all planned in advance, well organised and well prepared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you understand Dario Kordic to be in terms of his position or role, if you will, in the community, in Central Bosnia at that time, in April 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: I know he was the president of the HDZ. The Croat people saw their god in him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you understand him to have any particular relationship with Mate Boban? Again, I don't necessarily mean a personal or family relationship, but any other association that you were aware of with Mr. Boban.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you understand about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: I think that they cooperated, pursued the HDZ policy in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you heard about, around this time, something called the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: I did. It was an organised community of Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you understand Mr. Kordic and Mr. Boban to fit into any structure, if you will, related to Herceg-Bosna? What role did they have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: I think they were right at the top, amongst the leadership.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Moving on, then. Witness AQ, do you recall that throughout the Easter time period there was electricity or power, if you will, available?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court whether that was different than what had been the situation during the Muslim holidays of Ramadan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: During Ramadan, we had shortages in the supply of power.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm for the Court, Witness AQ, that there were times, to your knowledge, when the power to the Bosniak or Muslim villages would be cut off, but the power, electricity, to the Croat villages would continue?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Directing your attention, then, still on the 15th of April, the same day as what you saw on television, is it correct, Witness, that your husband was on guard duty in Ahmici, and that the village guard consisted of two men each on two-hour shifts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 15th of April, your husband was on guard duty with an 18-year-old man named Kermo Elvedin; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They had the shift from approximately 10.00 that evening until midnight; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your husband, and, to your knowledge, the other Muslim men involved with guard duty, did not carry a gun while on guard duty; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the main, the village guard was nothing very organised, but essentially would be two Muslim men walking through the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your husband and Kermo came back to the house, that is, your house, at about 11.30 that evening to smoke a cigarette with you. After the three of you had smoked about half a cigarette, you heard a sound that sounded like something between a gunshot and a hand grenade exploding; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You and your husband and Kermo knew that there were no BiH soldiers in the area, so you suspected that the sound must have come from an HVO dugout or trench in the area of Sutra. Your husband and Kermo left the house, went in the direction of Sutra, again, where the sound seemed to have come from; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, there was a changing of the guards from one shift to the next. Kermo went home and your husband returned to your home; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You asked your husband about the sound. He said he didn't know what it was, but he had seen a large number of HVO soldiers in the dugout, which, he indicated to you, based on his previous guard duty experience, was unusual; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He also reported to you about that time, when he returned to the house, that he had been able to see through a window into the basement of Ivica Kupreskic's house, and in the basement, there were a lot of HVO soldiers gathered there with weapons and in uniform.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the usher to hand to you and distribute Exhibit Z1553.1, which won't take very -- again, quite quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Perhaps for purposes of identification, since it shows a particular location, it should not be on the ELMO. We'd ask ultimately, Your Honour, that these exhibits be under seal, because they do tend to identify the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you'll allow me, Witness AQ, in the interests of time, there is a key or legend attached as part of this exhibit -- again, 1553.1 -- and the item marked as number 3 on the map, or aerial, can you confirm to the Court that that is your house where you lived on the 15th and morning of the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Item number 1 is Ivica Kupreskic's house, where your husband indicated he had seen a number of HVO soldiers gathered in the basement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Item number 2 is the area of a dugout where, again, he said he had seen more HVO soldiers than usual; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, the rest of the exhibit basically speaks for itself, with the legend attached, unless there's some further question about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AQ, can you confirm to the Court that there were no BiH army or Territorial Defence formations, units, or positions in Ahmici on the 15th and 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: There were none.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were no attacks by any BiH or TO forces in the area, to the best of your knowledge, and in fact, the area was peaceful up to the moment of the HVO attack. Is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your husband, however, continued to have misgivings that something bad was going to happen, perhaps not that night, but that trouble was, in fact, building to some bad point. You talked about, in fact, the two of you that night, what to do if something happened or if one of you was killed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you told your husband that, really, it was crazy to talk of such things.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct, Witness, that you then went to bed, you and your husband went to bed about 12.30 a.m. on now the 16th of April, turned on the television? You fell asleep at that point, perhaps both of you did. You woke up some time later. The television was still on. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you woke up and looked at the television that was still on, what did you see on television?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: When I looked at the TV, I saw the same programme that was being broadcast and rebroadcast all day, where Kordic was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was when Mr. Kordic was making the speech.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After another several hours, you and your husband woke up and heard someone in the yard or garden of the house. You could hear gunshots and people cursing the Muslims and shouting obscenities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your husband went to the front door to go outside, but as soon as he touched the doorknob, there was an explosion at the door. You could see your husband then holding his stomach and his hands covered in blood. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'll try to move through this quite quickly, but if you do feel that you have to take a pause, please indicate. Then there was a lot of shooting, and somebody apparently shot through the door and hit your husband in the chest. You were later able to see that he had been shot in the chest, and there was actually an exit wound in his back; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About that time, you looked at the clock, and it was 5.30 in the morning on the 16th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that point you gathered your son, aged three and a half at the time, your sister-in-law, who was about 20 or 21 years old, who was also living with you in the house; you gathered them together with you in the house. The house continued to be attacked with shooting and hand grenades being thrown into the house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You tried to tend to your husband but, unfortunately, really there was nothing you could do except wash his face; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he died a short time later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Usher, if I could have your assistance, please, for a moment. If I could tender Exhibit Z1553.2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AQ, is that a photograph of your husband who was killed the night or morning of April 16th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Except for a pistol, is it true, ma'am, that there were no guns or military weapons in your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court -- at any time during the attack on your house that evening and the murder of your husband, please tell the Court whether there was any shooting or military or defensive action coming from your house at any time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: There was none.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At one point, the shooting into the house was so intense that your sister-in-law lay on the floor, covering your three-and-a-half-year-old son to protect him from being hit. You then proceeded, yourself, to lay your body over two of them in an attempt to protect both of them, and at that point, is it fair to say, Witness, that you were sure that all of you would be killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, you and your son and your sister-in-law were able to escape from the house, out the window. You then encountered several groups of HVO soldiers. At one point, you and, actually, I should say, your son and sister-in-law were forced to run in front of a group of HVO soldiers in the direction of where the HVO soldiers claimed there were BiH soldiers; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In effect, they were putting you, your son, and your sister-in-law between them and what they claimed again to be the position of BiH soldiers as they moved along; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this time, once you had escaped from the house and were making your way at various points, you saw two HVO soldiers throw hand grenades into Suad Ahmic's house. The HVO soldiers then took a cow out of his stable and set the stable on fire; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, Witness AQ, that on the 16th of April, only the Muslim houses in Ahmici were destroyed or substantially damaged; all of them, in fact, were on fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes, totally destroyed, all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you observe that day about the status or condition of the Croat homes in the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: All the Croat houses were intact. They were not damaged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct, Witness, that no Bosniaks were left in Ahmici after the HVO attack on the 16th, and in fact, as of at least November 1997 -- perhaps later but at least as of November 1997 -- there were still, to your knowledge, no Bosniaks living in the village and all the Bosniak houses remained essentially destroyed? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Final question, Witness. By the end of the day on the 16th of April, 1993, what did you think then of the broadcast that you'd seen by Mr. Kordic on the 15th of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: I concluded that indeed all his threats came true. His call to an uprising to destroy the Muslims, unfortunately all this was true. I could not believe that this would happen, but it proved to happen all after.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No further questions. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The witness is a victim in terms of what happened on that critical day, and there is no need for the Defence to remind her of that. Since the Court already had ample opportunity to hear what happened to this witness, the Defence of Mr. Kordic will not have any questions for her unless, of course, the Court has some questions to address to the Defence in this connection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The one matter which it may be right for you to put to the witness is if you challenge that the accused Dario Kordic made the television broadcast inviting the Croat people to rise against the Muslim forces. If that's challenged, she should have the opportunity of dealing with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I just remind you of the fact that you had the opportunity of seeing Z665. That is a videotape. There's also its transcript that has been admitted into evidence. I did not want to challenge it now, because it's quite evident from this transcript, which is quite comprehensive, what Mr. Kordic actually meant and said. However, if it is necessary, I'm going to put it to the witness too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It may be that the simplest way to deal with it is this: Witness AQ, is it your recollection that this is what Dario Kordic said on television on that occasion, that he was inviting the Croat people to rise up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes, quite, quite clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, that's sufficient. Cross-examined by Mr. Mikulicic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good day, Witness AQ. I'm sorry we cannot see each other properly. My name is Goran Mikulicic, and I am Defence counsel for the second accused, together with Mr. Kovacic. I'm going to put a few questions to you, and I'd kindly ask you to answer them to the best of your recollection. First of all, please accept my sincere condolences for everything that happened to you in the village of Ahmici in 1993. Witness AQ, you said that in September 1992, you came to the witness and lived in it. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before that day did you come to the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you knew the villagers from Ahmici mostly, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes, in part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until April 1993 and everything that happened then, did you get to know them a bit better perhaps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, madam, when were village guards first organised in that village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I really cannot remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us try to orient ourselves in time. There was a conflict in October 1992 in Ahmici. Do you know that there was a roadblock by the village of Ahmici at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the placement of that roadblock was the immediate cause of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your husband have anything to do with the placement of that roadblock?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether there were any military weapons and military units in the village in October 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: No. I'm not aware of that. Throughout that day of the attack we were at home, and in the evening when we tried to pull out towards the village when the shooting subsided, we did not meet anyone on the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know that in the village there was a company that belonged to the Territorial Defence otherwise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're sure that it didn't exist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AQ, if I were to tell you that during this trial, before this Court several dozen persons testified before this Court, villagers from Ahmici and Territorial Defence commanders from the BH army who said there was a Territorial Defence company in Ahmici, and that they also gave the name of the commander of that company, what would you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: I don't want to go into all of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AQ, are you familiar with the military structure of the HVO at that time in the Vitez pocket?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: The only thing I know is that Blaskic was the commander-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the military units that operated in the area at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I imagine you also do not know which units participated in the attack of Ahmici in April 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: In April? On the 16th of April when this happened, afterwards I found out that the unit called Jokeri took part in it, I think. I don't know about the rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally manage to recognise any one of the attackers or did you see the insignia on their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: No, I did not recognise anyone. All of them were masked. Their faces were masked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said in your statement to the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor that some of the attackers asked whose house was which house in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: They asked me personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you conclude, on that basis, that these were persons who were not familiar with the local situation in the village of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: I don't think that it was someone who came from the outside. I think they were being led by persons who knew Ahmici very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If that is correct, why would they ask you then whose house is which house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: For camouflage purposes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That evening, before the attack on the 15th of April, you said that you watched television. That means that there was electricity all night in the village, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes, as opposed to other days, which was unusual. Four or six hours a week.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's leave that aside. I'm sorry. Were telephones also operating?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that your late husband was --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I would like to correct myself. You didn't use the right word for my "late husband." You're supposed to say "rahmetli." If I say that the Croat died, I use the word "pokojni," "May God rest his soul." I think that you shouldn't say "pokojni" when you refer to my late husband; you should say "rahmetli" as for Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, I apologise. I meant no disrespect whatsoever, but this is the first time I hear of this word.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: The first time?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, the first time. How did I hear of the "late" in the respect of "pokojni"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I know this is very difficult, but I think we'll get on more quickly if we don't argue. Mr. Mikulicic, have you got much more for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AQ, is it true that your husband was a member of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us from which date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: From the beginning of the aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which unit he belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: The 325th Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that he was on guard duty that night.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether I understood you correctly. Did he have weapons or did he not have weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your husband did not have any weapons in the house where he lived with you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Well, he had a pistol, the one that we had before too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he went on guard duty, he did not even take that pistol?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: No. No, he did not. He wore civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AQ, who ordered your husband to go on guard duty that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: I think they were organised in some way, after those events in Zenica, I think. However, I don't know for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AQ, do you know a person called Midhat Berbic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that he was commander of the TO company in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: I really don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Hazrudin Bilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that he was commander of the platoon that was down at the main road by Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: I don't know. I lived in the middle part of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that you lived in the middle part of the village, between Upper and Lower Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. So do you perhaps know Nermin Kermo, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that he was commander of the platoon in the middle part of the village where you lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: I doubt it. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness has said that she knows nothing about the Territorial Defence in the village, if there was one. So there's really no point going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AQ, let us finish with this subject. Let us just clarify. You don't know anything about the structure of the HVO army or the structure of the BH army in Ahmici at that time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AQ, I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Just for the purposes of the transcript, I would like to draw your attention to D190/1, which speaks of the units of the BH army in Ahmici. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very briefly, Your Honour, if I could, in light of the Court's questions and Mr. Naumovski's questions about the broadcast. I'm looking at specifically, for the LiveNote purposes, page 26, starting at line 11. Re-examined by Mr. Scott:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you these follow-up questions, if I could, Witness AQ. You testified that you saw different speeches by Mr. Kordic on the 15th of April, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Throughout the course of the day, just so we understand it correctly, throughout the course of the day, there appeared to you to be two or more speeches by Mr. Kordic which were being broadcast --

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You know, we can't get on with this constant interruption. Now, we will get clarified what the witness said. As I understood it, Mr. Scott, the witness said that she identified the speech which she had heard as that which is shown on the tape, Z665. Now, we can't really go behind that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour -- I'm sorry. If the Court allows. Your Honour, she also said, however, she said -- I asked the follow-up question about were there different speeches by Mr. Kordic being broadcast that day, and she said at line 21, "Different speeches."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, then, are we saying that the speech which she is talking about is the speech on 665, or are we saying it's a different one? It places the Court in an impossible position with evidence of this nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's exactly the reason for my preceding clarification, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let me try and understand. Witness AQ, you were shown or you listened to a tape when you were here. As I understood it, that was the tape to which you were referring when you gave evidence about this broadcast that you had seen on the 15th of April. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Any more questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I thank the Court for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness AQ, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the International Tribunal to give it. You are free to go. Just wait until the blinds have come down. Mr. Nice, it's about the time for our break, but have you got an application in respect of the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Nice, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I have. It is set up at the beginning of his summary, and as the Court will appreciate, this is a witness who has, in fact, given evidence before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We better make sure that we're talking about the same witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: He's a witness who did give evidence earlier in open session, and he explains in paragraph 1 of the summary why his position is changed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I haven't got this. Are we in private session yet?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Pseudonym for this witness is AS. Sorry, AR.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Take a seat. Examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have been granted protection by the Chamber so that your name will not be revealed, and you will be known throughout your testimony as Witness AR. Will you look at this piece of paper. Without reading the name on it, just simply say, "Yes" if it is your name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Resident in Busovaca, did you mobilise in the Territorial Defence in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the JNA left the Busovaca barracks, I think at Kaonik, in May 1992, to whom did they want to hand those barracks over?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: The TO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the HVO agree with that plan and proposal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were negotiations attempted by, amongst others, Hadzimejlic and Merdan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who for the HVO was making the decisions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: May I -- may I offer an explanation to clarify this question or, rather, my answer?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Florijan Glavocevic came to negotiate on behalf of the Croats, because he said that Dario Kordic was not there and that they could not take any decision without him, and they invited him to the negotiations in Busovaca, to the crisis staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that Hadzimejlic and Merdan were arrested. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: That was the information we received when Hadzimejlic returned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereabouts did you understand they'd been detained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: They were to conduct the negotiations at the crisis staff in Busovaca, but according to him, the HVO police met him in front of the crisis staff in Busovaca and took them to Tisovac, which is a outing area near Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there, subsequently, a position taken by the HVO about the weapons of those in the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes. Before that, they were asking the Territorial Defence to hand down their weapons and withdraw from Busovaca, but when Hadzimejlic came from those so-called negotiations, they allowed the Territorial Defence to withdraw with their armament but to withdraw from Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we've heard a lot about paragraph 4, so I haven't deal with it, save to say to the witness:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You could, if asked, deal with the destruction of shops in Busovaca with the loss of jobs and with the limited movement of Muslims in that area? You could, if asked, deal with those topics?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 27th of October of 1992, were you on your way to a command post in Kacuni, to which the Territorial Defence had been moved, when you were stopped in front of the Hotel Tisa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to you, your car, and your weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: In front of the Tisa hotel we were stopped by two members of the HVO police, and they wanted to search our vehicle and us. They saw that I had an official handgun, a pistol. I had all the papers from the Territorial Defence. They requested that I hand them over that weapon and said that it will be returned back to me the next day. However, they did not give me any paper or any document that they had seized it. So the next day I went to their commander, Pasko Ljubicic, in the Vitez Hotel, and he issued me a certificate, but I was not returned my weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you understand that what happened to your weapon had happened to other people's weapons in a similar way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 6 has been covered elsewhere. Paragraph 7 of the summary and down to the end of the witness's personal treatment I'll deal with by leading, unless I'm told otherwise. On the 24th of January, were you and your father arrested by the HVO military close to the UNPROFOR base when you were in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indeed, Territorial Defence had been forbidden to wear uniforms at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Both uniforms and weapons. We did not wear them in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you taken first to the bus station where you were detained, and your requests to speak to the police chief Vlado Cosic were denied?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With some 10 to 15 other men, were you taken to Kaonik camp where there were already some 250 people at the time of your arrival, with more coming in following days, so that the total number was about 430?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: I was taken to the Kaonik camp, but that figure of 250 is not correct. There were about 20 of us, but within the next day or two they were bringing in people, so that it rose to 250, and by the end of that fortnight there were 430 of them. There were not 250 of them when we were brought there, because we were amongst the first to be taken there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were most of the men at Kaonik civilians and certainly in civilian clothing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they all of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you compelled to go and dig trenches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Including at the front lines at Kula?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes. Kula, Podjele, Solakovici. Those are the places they took me, but other people were taken other places as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When digging trenches, you were denied water for 36 hours and food. You were beaten, your ribs were broken, your property was confiscated, you were forced to eat dinars because they hadn't been taken from you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes. It happened at Kula.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Faik Sarajlic struck with a rifle butt and his hat set on fire and replaced on his head?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to Podjele, did you also go to Prosje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that to dig trenches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see a man called Mehmed Beslic and another man called Zehrudin Dzafic, both of whom had serious head wounds after beatings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but that happened at Kula. We were all badly beaten at Kula, about 20 of us; however, Zehrudin Dzafic and Mehmed Beslic fared the worst.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear of the death, while digging trenches, of two men, Nermin Elezovic and Jasmin Sehovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: It wasn't while we were digging. They came to replace us at Kula, and we were taken back to our cells, and the next day we learned that they had been killed at that same place where we had dug trenches at Kula.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 15. Did you know a man called Anto Sliskovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in a position to recognise his voice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise his voice when you were at the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was Sliskovic's attitude to politics of the time? Was he liberal, moderate, or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: I knew him from before the war. He was rather nationalistic, chauvinistically-minded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doing such things as what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Well, for instance, when intoxicated, he would sing Ustasha songs in coffee shops, insult, verbally abuse various people, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that he was doing this, what were the relations between Muslims and Croats generally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: They were flexible at the time because Busovaca is a mixed environment, so that we looked after one another. And, of course, one could keep in touch with normal people, talk to them, socialise with them, work with them. It was a couple of years before the war, perhaps a year or two before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was, if anything, known by you of Sliskovic's relationship with Kordic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: The relationship between the two of them, it is difficult to define it, but it is evident that Sliskovic also worked for that same Herceg-Bosna, which was headed by Dario Kordic, and he must have held some important post, but I couldn't tell you which one exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean Sliskovic must have held an important post or Kordic must have held an important post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Kordic held a more important post. But Sliskovic also must have been rather high up; one could deduce that from his status.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you'd recognised the voice of Sliskovic at the camp. Were there reports -- paragraph 15 -- in relation to a man called Senad Lusija?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Did you hear of something that happened to a man called Senad Lusija at the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. One night, as my cell was next to the front door to the camp, I heard how they interrogated Senad Lusija and how they beat him, and it was then that I recognised Ante Sliskovic's voice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Apart from Kordic, was there anyone superior to Kordic, to your knowledge, in the area in Croat affairs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you acquainted with -- did you see Kordic wearing a uniform at any time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From roughly when, can you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: As of the proclamation of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna onwards. I could not give you the exact date, but on various occasions, yes, I saw him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have or give himself any rank, that you can remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: I don't know who conferred the rank upon him. However, in the media, and from some Croats -- or, rather, Catholics who had begun calling themselves Croats, I heard that he had been promoted to the rank of General. But who was it that promoted him, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time of the disarming of the Muslims and the separation of the communities, was there any need for that to happen in the town in which you lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Well, depends on how you look at it. In my view, there was no need for that because there were no military operations there; this was deep in the country, and there was no danger from the Serb or Chetnik aggressor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you wait there, please. You may be asked some further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Naumovski:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AR, allow me to introduce myself. I'm Mitko Naumovski, a lawyer from Zagreb, and with my colleague Steven Sayers, we represent Dario Kordic. I shall ask you several questions. I make the same mistake, so will you help me and please wait for a while after my questions so as to allow time for the interpreters to interpret it into the official languages of the Tribunal? Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A few introductory questions, Witness AR. You used to work for the Mediapan factory in Busovaca, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When new political parties were founded, you actively participated in the foundation of the Party for Democratic Action in Busovaca, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were a member of the SDA, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes, but I joined it only after a certain period of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. After the TO staff for the municipality of Busovaca was founded, and we know that Husein Hadzimejlic was its commander, would you agree that you were appointed the commander of the company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Shall we agree that it was the 3rd Company of the Busovaca detachment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
